text:
The Philadelphia Flyers arrive in Columbus at the end of the loudest week of their season. On Tuesday, ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported that Matvei Michkov would prefer a fresh start elsewhere. General manager Danny Brière flew to Edmonton, met with Michkov and his agent, and told reporters the report "was not correct," per PhillyVoice; The Athletic's Kevin Kurz reported that Michkov has not requested a trade. Then Rick Tocchet defended his handling of Michkov's ice time, and PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor argued that Tocchet's version doesn't tell the whole story of the first 11 games. Michkov is 21, a pending restricted free agent, and by our numbers Philadelphia's likeliest scorer tonight (27%).

The awkward part is that the Flyers have played better than their record says. They sit at a minus-21 goal difference on chances worth minus-15, and they've scored 9.8 fewer goals than those chances usually produce. O'Connor found another way to say it: ten losses already in games they led or were tied in the third period, in 21 games. This is the last stop of a five-game road trip they're 1-1-2 on.

Columbus is in a quieter kind of trouble. The Blue Jackets are winless in three, outscored 12-4, and our numbers say that's partly real: they had 46% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, in those games. Jet Greaves has lost his last five starts with an .858 save rate, 3.6 goals worse than expected. He was 15 goals better than expected last season, so this is a slump from a goalie with a track record, not a verdict. Mathieu Olivier is one goal from 50 for his career.

It's a division game between the seventh and eighth teams in the Metropolitan, two points apart. Our numbers give Philadelphia a 4% chance at the playoffs and Columbus 9%, so neither can afford many more nights like this week. The last meeting went to Columbus 4-3 in overtime on Oct. 27, in a game the Blue Jackets deserved to win only 19% of the time.
headline: Flyers bring the Michkov noise to Columbus
